newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Delay feared in setting up Angola unity government.
newsitem.headline: Delay feared in setting up Angola unity government.

text.p: Envoys of three countries involved in the Angolan peace process conferred with the president of the Security Council on Wednesday amid fears the inauguration of a unity government this weekend might be postponed, a council source said.

Representatives of the United States, Russia and Portugal discussed the situation with council president Hisashi Owada of Japan. They agreed the full council should consult further if a joint commission meeting in Luanda on Friday set a new date for the scheduled Jan. 25 inauguration, the source said.

The delay could result from uncertainty over the role in the government of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi and differences over the extension of government administration into areas held by the former rebel group.
The inauguration of a government of national unity and reconciliation would mark a high point in carrying out a 1994 accord ending nearly two decades of civil war in Angola.
A 7,000-strong U.N. peacekeeping force which has been helping implement the process is due to complete its mandate at the end of February.
